title: Labels, Selectors & Annotations
intro: Almost everything in Kubernetes finds its targets through labels, not names. Let's use them deliberately instead of just relying on them working automatically.

steps.prompt: Show all pods along with their labels.
steps.fake_output:
NAME      READY   STATUS    LABELS
web-abc   1/1     Running   app=web,env=prod,tier=frontend
db-0      1/1     Running   app=db,env=prod,tier=backend
steps.explanation: Labels are just key-value tags — Services, Deployments, and NetworkPolicies all use them to decide which pods they apply to.
steps.why: Without --show-labels, 'get pods' hides this entirely — you'd have to describe each pod one at a time to see its labels otherwise.

steps.prompt: Find only the pods labeled tier=frontend.
steps.explanation: This is exactly the same selection logic a Service uses internally to decide which pods to route to.
steps.why: You could grep the --show-labels output instead, but -l does real server-side filtering — it scales to thousands of pods where grepping a full list wouldn't.

steps.prompt: Find pods in either 'prod' or 'staging' environments in one query.
steps.fake_output:
NAME      READY   STATUS    LABELS
web-abc   1/1     Running   env=prod
web-stg   1/1     Running   env=staging
steps.explanation: The 'in (...)' set-based syntax lets you match multiple values for one key in a single command instead of running it twice and merging results.
steps.why: Simple '-l key=value' can only match one exact value — set-based selectors ('in', 'notin', 'exists') are what you need once you're matching more than one possible value.

steps.prompt: Add an annotation to the 'web-abc' pod noting who deployed it, without touching its labels.
steps.explanation: Annotations and labels look similar but serve different purposes: labels are for selection/grouping, annotations are for arbitrary metadata that nothing selects on.
steps.why: You could technically cram this into a label instead, but Selectors would then start matching on it accidentally — annotations exist specifically so you can attach metadata that nothing queries against.
